summary: The migrated WinUI 3 app faithfully reproduces all three UWP scenarios. No genuine migration defects were found. The only discrepancies are measurement-tool artifacts, documented below so they are not mistaken for regressions.

toolingArtifacts.description: winapp UI screenshots of the WinUI 3 client area come back blank white (only the system-drawn title-bar buttons render). This is the known DirectComposition/Direct3D capture limitation: PrintWindow-based capture cannot read WinUI 3 composited content. The UIA tree is fully populated with correct control bounds and the controls respond with correct text output, proving content actually renders and functions.
toolingArtifacts.evidence: parity/winui3/screenshots/*.png are blank, yet 'winapp ui inspect -a 53496' shows the full visual tree (SampleTitle, ScenarioControl list, Description, buttons, outputBox) and button clicks produce real outputBox text.

toolingArtifacts.description: The original UWP app launched and rendered correctly (a real visual golden was captured for the landing scenario), but winapp's UI Automation cannot penetrate the UWP CoreWindow (hosted by ApplicationFrameHost): the UIA tree exposes only the top-level Pane. Therefore scenario navigation and control actuation on the UWP app were not possible, and no per-control behavioral golden exists. All UWP-side 'responded:false' values mean 'unreachable via UIA', NOT 'dead'. Consequently no behavioral downgrade can be asserted against the UWP.
toolingArtifacts.evidence: parity/baseline/ui/*.json show a single CoreWindow Pane (elementCount:1); parity/baseline/capture-manifest.json has navOk:false and responded:false for every action.

toolingArtifacts.description: Compare-Parity.ps1 graded Scenario 3 PARTIAL (coverage 3/4, actions 1/3 live). Manual investigation shows this is a false negative: (1) the ToggleSwitch is present and identical to the UWP source (lampToggle, OnContent 'Lamp On' / OffContent 'Lamp Off'); the structural matcher missed it only because it keys on the label 'Lamp On' while the toggle currently displays 'Lamp Off' (its off state) and is correctly DISABLED because no lamp device is present (hardware-gated, matching UWP). (2) The 'Register for AvailablityChanged Event' button IS functional: invoking it by AutomationId (btn-registerforavai-d10c) produces the correct 'Error: No lamp device was found' output; the harness's invoke-by-verbose-label simply failed to target it. (3) The disabled toggle is not a dead control - it is legitimately hardware-gated, which the parity skill says should be flagged for manual review, not failed.
toolingArtifacts.evidence: Scenario3_AvailabilityChanged.xaml is byte-identical between UWP source and WinUI migration; 'winapp ui invoke btn-registerforavai-d10c' returned 'Invoked ... via InvokePattern' and outputBox updated to the expected error; interactive inspect shows 'lampToggle Button "Lamp Off" [off] [disabled]'.

perScenario.note: Both buttons present and functional; outputBox shows 'Getting class selection string for lamp devices...' then 'No lamp device found' - correct on hardware without a lamp.
Both buttons present and functional; outputBox shows 'Initializing lamp' then 'No lamp device was found' - correct on hardware without a lamp.

Register/Unregister buttons functional (correct 'No lamp device was found' output); lampToggle present and correctly disabled (hardware-gated) - faithful to UWP. Harness PARTIAL was a structural/label false-negative, not a defect.
